RESULT: zero qualifying ideas for this lens. On <=2014 evidence, opening a KIS overseas futures/options account is not supported as a way to beat v1 on both bases. No backtest was computed; numbers below are registry values, published <=2013 sample values, or my inferences (labelled).

WHY (structural, inference): futures-account cash earns 0 and inter-broker transfers are manual (not allowed), so the futures account is a separate compounding pot. It raises total CAGR on a basis only if its own after-tax CAGR exceeds v1's on that basis: 16.16% (path), 31.08% (real NDX; about 52%/yr in 1986-99). For a stream with Sharpe S levered at fraction f of Kelly, log growth is about S^2(f - f^2/2). After 11% tax, real NDX needs S >= about 0.9 at half Kelly (0.78 at full Kelly); path needs only about 0.67 at half Kelly. That is why margin-light futures streams win path and lose real NDX, and why the D gate (1.1 early / 0.8 unseen) is the right yardstick. If the stream is worthless the loss is bounded by the account (a 15% slice is about -0.55pp/yr CAGR over 30 years).

Known stream Sharpes in this lens (<=2014): Treasury month-end futures .64-.95 (T18, about 0 in 1962-85), night-only 1x .22-.57 (X42), FOMC day .28 (T20), equity month-end liquidity cycle about .7 (my inference from published window means, not measured). None reaches 0.9 stand-alone.

ONE DECISION FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR (not listed as an idea because it repeats T18, which my task forbids): a month-end futures basket = T18's Treasury stream + the equity month-end liquidity cycle. If the two legs are uncorrelated the basket Sharpe would be about 1.0-1.1 (inference, unverified), the only arithmetic route in this lens that could reach the real-NDX bar. T18's own result file (research/c3_create/r9b/RESULT_R9B_KO.md, line 10) left a user decision open: whether to apply G1 to a margin-light Treasury calendar overlay and whether to allow total exposure above 3x. The user's new willingness to open a futures account may be that decision. My rough prior for a both-bases PASS of such a basket is about 5% (inference); it belongs with E05/X20 (other threads). Whole-contract sizing: 1 MNQ is about 70-84M KRW notional; at 3.3x leverage that needs about 23-25M KRW in the futures account, i.e. total capital of about 155-170M KRW at a 15% slice (MES is roughly two-thirds of an MNQ, so about 105-115M KRW; unverified live sizes). At the MS1 10M KRW start the book holds zero contracts and equals v1.

ideas.kill_type: A (CUT overlay), early window first; unseen opened once only if early passes
ideas.prereg_sketch: N=2 fixed variants, no tuning. Data: all original 10-Q/10-QSB and 10-K/10-K405/10-KSB main documents (no amendments, no exhibits) filed 1994-01..2014-12, rows after 2014-12-31 dropped at read time. Tone_i = (pos - neg)/words with the LM 2011 positive/negative lists. Because the HF data stores token ids, pre-register a token-level count (tokens whose decoded string is in the LM list, via numpy isin) and validate it once against full decoding on a fixed 2% sample (corr >= .95 required, else full decode). Monthly index = equal-weight mean over filings filed in month m, 4-month moving average (as in the paper), then z-score against the trailing 60 months (min 24) - real time, no full-sample standardization. Usable from the first trading day of month m+1, plus v1's 2-day delay. V1 (primary): z >= +0.5 -> v1 3x becomes 1x for month m+1. V2: same rule with tone computed only from filers with SIC 357x/367x/737x/48xx/283x (Nasdaq-like mix). Kill test A in 21-day blocks where v1 is at 3x: P(3x beats deposit | on) >= 10pp below the v1-3x base rate, >= 8 on-blocks, early window 1996-01..1999-12 (first usable month after burn-in) and unseen 2000-01-03..2014-12-31. No SPX 1955-85 coverage exists. Only a survivor goes to L.measure2 (FINAL PASS rule of the brief, N=2 deflation). First lane step before anything else: confirm monthly filing counts 2011-2014 in the data repo (the separate small index repo is thin there), stop if the unseen window is degraded.
ideas.non_dilution_argument: (1) No data before 1994 and a 24-month burn-in, so 1986-1995 is bit-identical to v1. (2) The only part of the 52%/yr era that can be touched is 1996-1999, and that is exactly the early kill window: the lane survives only if the flagged v1-3x blocks there had a hit rate at least 10pp below base. If optimistic tone coincided with the 1996-99 run-up (my expectation), the lane dies at the first test without ever reaching measure2. (3) The overlay cuts to 1x, not cash, and acts only in flagged months (target about 30% of v1-3x months), so the worst case is bounded and visible in the real-NDX row of measure2, which must be > 31.08% for a PASS. (4) No capital is moved to another sleeve; it is a pure state overlay on v1's own instruments. Remaining honest worry: a hit-rate pass with a magnitude loss (a few very large up-blocks cut) - measure2 real NDX is the guard.

ideas.automation: Fully automatic. Live signal: a daily job reads the EDGAR daily form index and the day's 10-K/10-Q main documents from sec.gov (free, no login; SEC asks automated clients for a declared user agent - a configuration choice for the user's program, proposal only), counts LM words, updates the monthly index on the first trading day of each month. Orders: the same TQQQ <-> 1x (QQQ) switch v1 already uses for its 1x state, through the Kiwoom REST US spot API. No manual step, no margin, no short, no options.
ideas.risks: Honest view: this will most likely fail. (a) The published result rests on 144 months and essentially one cycle (2007-09), with a persistent regressor; 9-month-horizon R2 of 27.1% shows it is a slow level signal. (b) v1 already sidesteps 2008 through its macro alarms, so the incremental value inside v1-3x blocks in 2000-14 may be near zero. (c) 1996-99 is the natural enemy of any contrarian sentiment signal; I put the early-window pass at about 12% (and with 8-12 on-blocks a pass can be luck), unseen pass given early about 25%, measure2 both-bases given kill-test pass about 40% -> about 1.5% overall. If it did pass, a path gain of roughly +1 to +2pp is plausible after switch costs and tax; probability-weighted that is about +0.02pp. (d) The LM word list was built in 2011 from 1994-2008 filings, so pre-2011 signals use an ex-post instrument: label NON-ACTUAL (instrument look-ahead). (e) Secular drift in filing language (risk-factor sections added mid-2000s) can fake a trend; the trailing 60-month z-score is the only defence. (f) Token-level counting is a proxy for the paper's measure. (g) Cost: about 60 GB streamed and scanned on shared 4 cores, several hours in 20-minute jobs; nothing may be left on disk with post-2014 rows. (h) The low-tone ADD side is deliberately excluded: pessimistic filings cluster mid-bear (2001-02, 2008), the same failure as T38.

false_negative_audit.summary:
All 21 listed result files exist and were read, plus /mnt/project-files/research/bottleneck/RESULT_TB_KO.md. Nothing was computed and no forbidden file was opened. 18 candidates were positive versus v1 on both dev250_path and real NDX 1986-2014 at their own measurement and were rejected by a side rule. None is a clean false negative that can be honestly re-tested on <=2014 data.

Three findings matter:

1. OV1-B (cuts filled at the next open) is the only strategy change that was pre-registered with N = 1 and is positive on both: path 16.84% vs 16.16% (paired d +0.35pp, win ratio .736), real NDX 31.81% vs 31.08%. It failed only the +0.5pp type-F bar. It stays positive under the +0.1pp/side stress (+0.16 / +0.37), but its 2008-14 contribution is negative and the cut-day night return in 2000-14 averaged 0.00%. It is the best honest below-bar candidate. A re-test cannot lift it; before it is reported, its unmeasured caveat (actual TQQQ open prints 2010-2014) should be measured.

2. The bond fill of v1's idle cash is the largest both-positive result: path d +3.8 to +5.2pp and real NDX +3.4 to +4.4pp for the ungated, FB0, FBmed and SLmed rows, with dd80 falling from 73% to 56-59%. On the written numbers the ungated row would clear the FINAL1 type-F and FINAL PASS letters. It was closed by regime side rules: drift0 path d of -1.05 (ungated) and -0.05 (SLmed), and time-shift null p of .065 to .75. The ungated gain is +8.29 in 2000-14 but only +0.21 in 1986-99 and +0.00 / +0.16 in the two SPX eras. This is a bet on the bond regime, not a measurement error. No <=2014 re-check can settle it; whether drift0 is binding is a policy decision.
